rationale: Across published cohorts of Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome (STISS; PSMD12 haploinsufficiency), limb and extremity findings are predominantly preaxial anomalies (such as preaxial polydactyly, triphalangeal or hypoplastic thumbs, and ectopic fingernails/onychoheterotopia) rather than severe anterior limb reduction defects (e.g., severe oligodactyly or intercalary/terminal limb deficiencies). Furthermore, the craniofacial dysmorphism described across cohorts is subtle and distinct from the dense generalized hypertrichosis and arched synophrys characteristic of Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS), as well as the broad, angulated thumbs and halluces defining Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome (RSTS). The consistent absence of severe anterior reduction defects, RSTS-defining broad angulated digits, and CdLS-defining dense hypertrichosis across all characterized STISS patients indicates that their presence strongly argues against a diagnosis of PSMD12-related STISS.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 24 additional unrelated patients with STISS carrying truncating SNVs or CNV deletions involving PSMD12, cardinal features included developmental delay, intellectual disability, speech delay, cardiac and renal anomalies, and preaxial hand abnormalities, alongside signs resembling interferonopathy/chilblains in some patients, without reports of severe limb reduction defects or classic CdLS/RSTS features.

source.title: Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome: expanding the clinical and molecular phenotype
source.quote: In addition to previously reported DD/ID, speech delay, cardiac and renal anomalies, we also confirmed preaxial hand abnormalities as a feature of this syndrome. Of note, 2 patients also showed chilblains resembling signs observed in interferonopathy.

evidence.text: Investigation of six patients from two families with inherited truncating PSMD12 variants revealed fully penetrant DD/ID, craniofacial dysmorphism, short stature, and skeletal and ectodermal anomalies (including ectopic fingernail/onychoheterotopia), but none demonstrated generalized dense hypertrichosis, severe limb reduction, or broad/angulated thumbs/halluces.

source.title: Does It Run in Your Family? Inherited Truncating PSMD12 Variants Broaden the Phenotypic Spectrum of Stankiewicz‐Isidor Syndrome
source.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A
source.quote: Portraying a completely penetrant condition with inter- and intra-familiar clinical variability, all individuals presented with developmental delay, intellectual disability, craniofacial, and skeletal anomalies. Novel findings in our cohort included unilateral ectopic fingernail, cholesteatoma, oligodontia, and the occurrence of an ovarian teratoma.

evidence.text: Characterization of a family with PSMD12 haploinsufficiency causing proteasome dysfunction revealed developmental delay, skin rash, and congenital uveitis, representing an autoinflammatory and neurodevelopmental phenotype devoid of classic CdLS or RSTS severe dysmorphic hallmarks.

source.title: Haploinsufficiency of PSMD12 causes proteasome dysfunction and subclinical autoinflammation
source.quote: Whole-exome sequencing was performed in members of a family with skin rash, congenital uveitis, and developmental delay... Our work expands the genotype and phenotype spectrum of PRAAS and suggests a bridge between the almost exclusively inflammatory phenotypes in the majority of PRAAS patients and the almost exclusively neurodevelopmental phenotypes in the previously reported Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact incidence and precise HPO spectrum of digit and limb anomalies across the international cohort of all compiled PSMD12-haploinsufficient patients?
new_directions.rationale: While preaxial anomalies (preaxial polydactyly, triphalangeal thumb, onychoheterotopia) are established, systematically quantifying the negative predictive value of missing anterior reduction defects or broad angulated digits will sharpen clinical diagnostic algorithms.

new_directions.question_text: Can a machine-learning facial phenotyping algorithm (e.g., GestaltMatcher) reliably discriminate STISS dysmorphism from classic CdLS and RSTS facial gestalt?
new_directions.rationale: Automated facial analysis could quantitatively verify that the facial gestalt of STISS lacks the defining eyebrows/synophrys and nasal features of CdLS, offering clinicians objective discrimination.
